g.text: You mentioned earlier you wanted to talk about the fact I don't really believe the Indifference is a "real god." Is now a good time?
The other day, you were asking me about conceptual embodiment, and about the Indifference. Is something bothering you?
Roathe is convinced that the Man in the Wall isn't a real god. That he's the product of "conceptual embodiment." What do you think?
Lyon, what's going on between you and Roathe? I've only gleaned bits and pieces.
I am unsure as any time is a "good" time to discuss the tangible problem this has caused me, Drifter.
There are a great many things bothering me, Drifter. The topic of the Indifference and conceptual embodiment, I fear, is merely one of them.
The issue at hand, Drifter, is that I do not know. If I knew the answer, I would not be tearing myself apart with such an internal debate.
I shall summarize, though I am shocked you have avoided his rants on the topic. He is quite overeager to share them at every opportunity.
But as such, now is therefore, as "good" a time as any. It intrigued me that you seemed to side with Roathe in your belief that the Indifference was not a true god.
Or potentially two, depending on how you wish to interpret the situation. Though I suppose that is indeed the heart of my dilemma.
However, I should... start at the beginning. You will not understand precisely why this particular topic is of such import to me if you do not have some context...
He believes that the Indifference is not a god of the Void, in any sense of the word, and was in fact crafted by Entrati and all those who interacted with it afterwards -
I am a Brother of Lua. I have dedicated my life to her worship. All my life, I have believed this.
- created it from the Void via what you know as "conceptual embodiment."
And throughout all my years since arriving to the church, I have held fast to my faith - to what has been the firm knowledge that my suffering, my pain, and my visions -
Much in the same way you created Duviri, I believe.
- have been in her service. Have been in her name. And have been for her purpose.
That was... until "Cardinal Dimanche" revealed himself to be Albrecht Entrati.
And he told us the truth of who he was, the tale of his misdeeds with the Void, and all that came of it. More specifically... all that came out of it.
Correct. He told us of the sneering thing that greeted him, of the fingers he retrieved from that place that resembled his laboratory.
He told us of his descent in the seriglass bell into the emptiness. Of the place that resembled his laboratory.
Moreover, he told us of the great dread he felt, knowing he had unleashed a thing that could follow him not just through space, but through time.
A god of nothingness. A thing that must be contained. A creature of which he had pieces, who would scratch at the walls to be freed.
A terrible and consuming god who was, and also was not, already free.
Time is... tangled, for someone such as I, in the state I am now in. It is hard to describe. I have made a poor attempt to explain this once, and I have failed miserably.
Time is... tangled, for someone such as I, in the state I am now in. It is hard to describe, and I am doing a miserable job of it.
I would prefer to explain the details of it another time, as that is not the point of what I am trying to get to the heart of this day.
But if you're hearing - or heard - Rell... I want to talk about it.
I do want to get into that, though...
I know. And I have been egregiously avoiding the topic. His name alone
I know I have been egregiously avoiding the topic, and I apologize. But it is liable to send me into a vision from which I am not sure I may recover easiliy.
I assure you, we will. I know I have been egregiously avoiding the topic, and I apologize. But it is liable to send me into a vision from which I am not sure I may recover easiliy.
I do not wish to once more have to cut this conversation short because I am unable to continue due to my own infirmities.
it brings images of a man in chains
I don't think I would call anyone who has had to endure what you have "infirm," Lyon.
Infirm is a terrible way to say "cursed with visions he didn't ask for." But suit yourself.
You know what you're capable of, so I'll follow your lead.
I appreciate the sentiment. But I know I am but a shattered stained glass window on the best of days. I stand here wondering where many of the pieces have gone.
Thank you. I marvel at your patience. I know I am but a shattered stained glass window on the best of days. I stand here wondering where many of the pieces have gone.
Each time I find one that I have lost, I am more liable to cut myself on the edges than I am to do myself any good seating it back in place.
Sometimes I wonder if it would not be better to become one of those truly empty-eyed Harrows I see in my mind's eye, stretching as far as my nightmares will allow.
Breathe, Lyon. Breathe. They aren't really there.
I - I'm sorry, Lyon. Focus on the screen. I'm here.
I know this is a horrible burden you've been asked to carry. And maybe it isn't right. But I don't know a way out.
You mean the world to Marie. You've become such a dear friend to me. I think even Roathe would miss you, though he won't admit it.
[Confess feelings.] It would break my heart if you let that happen to you, Lyon. I... I care about you.
that is where you are wrong
and they shall never leave me
Not without resorting to... to the unthinkable. Or to that.
You are cherished. You're loved. You have family and friends. Even if it might not feel like that all the time.
I - Surely, you jest. You cannot mean your words, after what you have just witnessed? Either you have lost your wits or your compassion has overcome your senses.
No one's. You don't need to suffer like this anymore. Let it go.
I know. I know it hurts. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry. Walk out of the room.
You aren't alone, Lyon. And you would be missed.
No, Lyon. I mean it. You mean the world to me, and all I wish is that I could somehow make you believe it.
I... maybe you're right. Maybe this isn't the right time.
if only it were so simple
these chains have been mine for so long
Turn around, and walk out of the room in your mind.
I see M. Necraloid, and I hear tales of M. Ordis, or M. Otak. I think of the empty Warframes with their thoughts pulled from their skulls.
Good. I am glad you have snapped out of your own momentary insanity. It must be contagious after all. Perhaps we take an intermission from this device, as I fear it has begun to rot your brain.
they will be there another time
this chamber of blood and chains
Thank you... but I wonder, for how long, before the grief would become just another burden that was easier to bear in time?
I must beg your forgiveness. There are moments where my lucidity fails me, and I despise when others witness them.
It would be so easy to surrender. To give up. To lay my agony at the altar of suffering and say no more.

It would be so easy to surrender. To give up. To lay my agony at the altar of suffering and say no more. Or to do far worse - to do that which many have worried I might with a blade in the great dark of the night.
There is... merely one issue, Drifter. How might I take your words as truth when I know you have spun falsehoods before?
While I am flattered, I fear my answer is quite simply and unequivocally no.
But it... is... not who I am. And it is not who I shall ever be. I am to remain as this... broken bulwark, this shattered shield...
I have caught you in a lie already. Though I do not know the purpose of this one, I fear you have already broken my ability to trust you.
Which I know is not entirely uncommon for me, however, I feel as though I should reply to this in some
Do you want to stop here? Or can you continue? I understand either way.
It's all right. I'm here for you. Are you going to be okay?
[Confess feelings.] Lyon, I... I care about you. I want to be here for you when you have these moments, if you'll let me.
Always to bleed, yet never to die...
So, while I am deeply flattered, I fear my answer is quite simply and unequivocally -
- in some clever fashion or at least in some manner that would seem fitting for the situation and not -
I am all right to continue, thank you. It has passed, as they always do. These... visions of mine are like clouds that pass over Lua. They can be total in their darkness, but they are often brief.
Yes, thank you. It has passed, as they always do. These... visions of mine are like clouds that pass over Lua. They can be total in their darkness, but they are often brief.
Surely, you jest. You cannot mean your words, after what you have just witnessed? Either you have lost your wits or your compassion has overcome your senses.
- and not give you the impression that it is not requited as that is very much not the case -
No, Lyon. I mean it. You mean the world to me, and all I wish is that I could somehow make you believe it.
I... maybe you're right. Maybe this isn't the right time.
We have wandered far from the point of this conversation, haven't we? I am so very sorry. You do not need to suffer such magniloquent, self-pitying maundering.
Lua on high... where was I?
Good. I am glad you have snapped out of your own momentary insanity. It must be contagious after all. Perhaps we take an intermission from this device, as I fear it has begun to rot your brain.
You have every reason to vent now and then. I'm glad you feel comfortable talking to me.
It's certainly not self-pitying. I would have to look up the other two to see if they hold true.
You were talking about the Indifference & Entrati. And how time has become less... linear for you, now.
Thank you. I try not to make my concerns the burdens of others when I can help it. But I appreciate the opportunity.
Would you like to "go out" with me? I'm not sure what they called in in your time. Courting, I suppose.
Quite. Yes. And to avoid the issue of it truly becoming circular, we will move past that point in the story, if you please.
Imagine my dismay when Entrati informed me, however, that the voices in my mind and the visions I had suffered my entire life were not the result of Lua -
- but the corruption of the Indifference upon the timeline.
But how could the Indifference go back to your year? And earlier, to your childhood?
Precisely what I asked him at the time. He explained to me the concepts of "quantum entanglement", "superposition" and "eternalism" -
He came with proof of his impossibilities. I knew he was Albrecht Entrati, not Cardinal Dimanche. But to say that all that I was - all that I believed - was the work of the Indifference?

I did not know what to believe, at first. He came with proof of his impossibilities. I knew he was Albrecht Entrati, not Cardinal Dimanche. But to say that all that I was - all that I believed - was the work of the Indifference?
And while it all made sense to me in a superficial, scientific way, I did not truly understand.
That I had prayed in service to a false god and to to Lua, all my years?
This is going to make my head hurt.
But the Indifference wasn't free yet in your time. But was he? In ours?
I did not know what to do. I still do not.
This is precisely the reason I attempt not to grapple with the specifics on most days...
And lo, you see the problem I face.
Matters grew far worse when Roathe arrived. For my crisis of faith became one layer more complicated when I learned that the Indifference is not a god at all -
Do you still wish to hear the situation between myself and Roathe? I fear it has become suddenly and laughably unimportant in my mind today.
- but a mere product of human hubris.
Sure. We'll have plenty of time later.
I could think of a better way to spend our time together...
I. Well. Yes. I. I do suppose. That is. That is
I am only a statue of flesh, fashioned in worship to false idols, designed only for suffering...
